plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompons, spiders, and daisy-like singles. It thrives in cool fall temperatures and tolerates light frosts, making it a staple of late-season gardens across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the national floral emblem of Japan, where the annual Chrysanthemum Festival honors it.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tropical and subtropical tree that is covered with clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. In late October, entire streets in the Southern Hemisphere turn purple as the petals carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of these trees, and a popular superstition in Australia holds that a jacaranda blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A tall, airy annual with delicate, feathery foliage and saucer-shaped flowers on slender stems. It blooms freely until the first hard frost, and in warmer regions such as the southern US and Mexico it keeps flowering through late October.
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; naturalized and cultivated in many temperate regions
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning 'harmony' or 'ordered universe', a reference to the balanced symmetry of its petals.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that is among the first camellias to bloom, producing fragrant, open flowers with prominent golden stamens from early autumn into winter. It is valued for its glossy foliage and for providing nectar to pollinators late in the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking and cosmetics in Japan.
